title: Operator trail retention & encryption playbook - Cobalt Consortium sync
summary: Cobalt Consortium and Redwood reviewed what operator/admin trails capture, how to export streams for SIEM, KMS integration options, and proposed retention/archival playbook for compliance. Agreed to pilot a nightly export to customer-owned S3 + send security pack. Action items and follow-up pilot timeline captured.
topics: scope of operator trails and admin events
encryption at rest/in transit and KMS/HSM options

transcript:
Header: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM) // Oliver (CISO), Sofia (Cloud), Marcus (Eng Mgr), Anika (Compliance)

Summary: Quick sync on operator trails - what we capture, export options, KMS integration and retention playbook. Conversation included SIEM ingestion patterns and legal hold considerations.

00:00 Jordan: alright good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, quick round of intros?
00:08 Oliver: Oliver Grant, I'm the CISO at Cobalt. we're mainly here to make sure anything we ship passes our SOC and ISO audits.
00:14 Sofia: Sofia, cloud architect, I'll own the bucket and the network side.
00:18 Marcus: Marcus, eng mgr, I'll be helping with agent setup and pipelines.
00:22 Jordan: great thanks. Priya is our SE, she'll walk through the operator trail payload and exports.
00:30 Priya: hi all, so operator trails is essentially a compact event stream: user actions, role changes, service account tokens, model deployment events, API key lifecycle events, and system-level admin ops, we capture metadata like actor, actor_ip, resource, action, timestamp, request_id and diff payload when available.
00:55 Marcus: when you say "diff payload" is that full request body or a delta?
01:01 Priya: usually a delta; full payloads are optional and gated by config because of PII concerns. we sometimes have imperfect transcription on longer payload fields in the UI export, we've seen the model names get mangled as "red wood" or similar in auto transcription.
01:18 Oliver: for compliance we need an append-only trail, tamper evidence, and chain of custody. what does Redwood provide here?
01:25 Priya: trails are write-once in the internal store; for customer-proof we provide signed export bundles with checksums. for live integrations the recommended pattern is streaming export to customer SIEM via syslog or Kinesis/Kafka or batched nightly exports to customer-owned S3/GCS.
01:48 Sofia: network wise we'd prefer S3 encrypted with our KMS key, so Redwood never has unencrypted copies in transit or rest. do you support customer-managed KMS (HSM backed)?
01:57 Priya: yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for hosted we support envelope encryption with customer KMS keys (bring-your-own-kms) and key rotation policies. there are two patterns: direct-write by Redwood to your S3 using your IAM role, or Redwood pushes an encrypted bundle to our staging then you pull. direct write avoids staging.
02:25 Marcus: any TLDR on formats? Splunk vs JSONL vs protobuf?
02:30 Priya: JSONL by default, with an optional protobuf binary payload for compactness. Splunk ingestion usually uses a forwarder reading JSONL. Kafka topics are available for high-throughput orgs.
02:45 Anika: retention windows: our legal needs 7 years for certain records, but we'd like a hot-window for 90 days and cold archive for 7 years. can Redwood tier retention?
02:56 Jordan: yes we can recommend hot/cold tiers. Redwood's platform lets you set retention rules per-event-type (e.g., auth events 2 years, config changes 7 years). long-term archival typically uses immutable S3 with versioning + Object Lock for legal hold.
03:12 Oliver: object lock sounds good. how do you prove immutability for auditors?
03:17 Priya: we provide manifest + SHA256 checksums for each object and an audit manifest that records export job id, start/end times, and signer identity. we can also export a verification script auditors can run to validate checksums.
03:36 Marcus: what about RBAC and SSO correlation? we use SAML Okta and need user_id mapping to our internal directory.
03:42 Priya: trails include external_id fields so you can correlate SAML subject (nameid) to internal user id. we also log session start/stop and SSO token issuance events. sometimes the transcription labels tokens as "SS O" or similar in auto transcripts so watch for that when sampling.
04:02 Oliver: is there a latency SLA for streaming exports? in a security incident we want near-real-time events in our SIEM (sub-30s).
04:08 Jordan: for Dedicated and Private deployments we can provide low latency streaming with SLOs. Hosted can do near-real-time too but latency depends on batching policies; we have a "push" mode with small batches that targets <30s but cost is higher.
04:28 Sofia: for pilot we want encrypted nightly exports to our S3 plus a lightweight stream into our Splunk for critical auth events.
04:35 Priya: recommended approach: 1) critical auth and policy-change events -> streaming Kafka topic -> Splunk forwarder; 2) full operator trail -> nightly JSONL export to your S3 with Object Lock + KMS.
04:52 Anika: audit trails need to include admin console UI changes and API operations; can you capture who pressed buttons and also the resulting system state?
04:59 Priya: we capture user action and diff payload when enabled. for some change workflows we capture before/after snapshots but that's opt-in because of size. for high-fidelity compliance you can enable full snapshots for select resources.
05:18 Marcus: how do we handle redaction for PII in exports?
05:22 Priya: redwood has configurable redaction rules at export time; you can scrub fields or replace with tokens. the schema includes a field-level sensitivity tag so you can route redactable fields to a different export path.
05:36 Oliver: what about proof of rotation for KMS keys? auditors ask for rotation timelines and evidence.
05:41 Jordan: we log key-rotation events, key usage, and can include rotation metadata in the export manifest. if you're using your KMS we rely on your KMS audit logs combined with our manifest for correlation.
05:57 Sofia: network/firewall: if Redwood writes directly to our S3, what IAM pattern do you use?
06:02 Priya: assume-role with an ARN you grant to Redwood's exporter principal. read-only put-object permissions scoped to the bucket/prefix with SSE-KMS key condition. we can do VPC endpoints to avoid traversal over the public internet.
06:22 Marcus: does Redwood sign the export artifacts?
06:25 Priya: yes, we sign manifests with an exporter key and include checksums; there's also an option for PGP signing if you prefer.
06:35 Anika: during legal hold we must freeze deletion. can you support temporary override of retention rules for specific records?
06:42 Jordan: yes, we support hold flags per export bundle that prevent lifecycle deletion. holds can be time-boxed or indefinite until released by an authorized role.
06:55 Oliver: curious on cost tradeoffs: streaming critical events vs. full retention for 7 years. any guidance?
07:02 Jordan: typical pattern is keep critical events streaming (higher cost) for 90 days in hot storage, then bundle and cold-archive at lower cost. full snapshots can be expensive; we typically recommend differential snapshots + delta replay for long-term needs. Redwood Optimize can also estimate incremental cost per retention policy.
07:30 Marcus: any integrations with our SIEM vendor? we use Splunk and an internal analytics lake.
07:34 Priya: Splunk via forwarder/HTTP Event Collector, direct S3 ingestion for long-term analytics, Kafka for real-time. we have sample configs in the security docs.
07:48 Sofia: we need to validate that exported artifacts are complete and unmodified; is there a verification tool?
07:53 Priya: yes, we provide a verification CLI that checks manifest signatures and object checksums against an export. auditors like that.
08:05 Oliver: ok sounds good. let's outline next steps for the pilot.
08:09 Jordan: recap - Jordan to send export schema and security pack; Priya to demo S3 export pipeline; Cobalt to share bucket/KMS details; pilot kickoff next week.
08:20 Oliver: agreed. last question: do you keep admin API access logs separate for internal SRE access? we need split of user vs service account activity.
08:29 Priya: yes, trails include actor_type (human|service) and we can create filtered exports for service accounts.
08:39 Marcus: minor note - we've seen a tiny mismatch in event timestamps by a second or two when crossing timezones; is timezone normalized to UTC?
08:46 Priya: all trails are normalized to UTC with ISO-8601 timestamps.
08:51 Anika: thanks everyone.
08:53 Jordan: thanks all we'll follow up with the documents and schedule.

End of transcript.
